text:
A low-carbohydrate intake can deplete glycogen stores and cause fatigue, especially during high-intensity exercise, while promoting fat oxidation and potentially aiding weight loss. It may cause short-term side effects like headaches and constipation and, if sustained, risks inadequate fiber and micronutrient intake unless carefully planned. Overall, it can be effective for specific goals but requires monitoring for nutritional adequacy and individual tolerance.
CONFIDENCE: 85
